options.label: Proceed as planned (3 tasks, 2 waves)
pros: Clean separation of concerns: T01 = model/schema, T02 = seed data, T03 = frontend guards
T02 and T03 run in parallel in Wave 1, maximizing concurrency
Each task has a single responsibility — easier to review, test, and roll back independently
Follows established project pattern where seed logic is separate from model changes
T02 has its own acceptance criteria (password, credits, idempotency, no collection reassignment) distinct from T01's schema concerns
cons: T02 is small (~20 lines of changes in 1 file) — overhead of a separate task context may feel disproportionate
Wave 1 parallelism between T02 and T03 saves little wall-clock time since T02 is very fast to implement
Slightly more orchestration overhead (3 developer handoffs instead of 2)

options.label: Merge T02 into T01 (2 tasks, 2 waves)
pros: T01+T02 combined is still a reasonably scoped task (model change + seed entry in one pass)
The seed logic directly exercises the new role column — testing them together gives faster feedback
Wave 1 becomes T03-only, which is fine since T03 is the heaviest task and cannot parallelize with anything anyway
cons: Merges two distinct concerns (schema vs. data seeding) into one task — muddies responsibility
T01 already touches 5 files; adding seed logic and its 5 acceptance criteria increases review surface
Loses the ability to run T02 and T03 in parallel (marginal impact given T02's small size)
Seed-specific edge cases (guest password, no collection reassignment) may get less focused testing attention inside a larger task

options.label: Block/defer F139
pros: Avoids introducing role-based access before a full RBAC design is finalized
cons: No technical blockers exist — all dependencies (auth, seed-users, frontend Layout, i18n) are in place
Feature scope is narrow and well-defined (2 role values, no permission matrix)
The guest user is explicitly requested for demo/sharing purposes — deferring blocks a user need
The role column defaults to 'admin', so backward compatibility risk is negligible

rationale: Option A (proceed as planned, 3 tasks / 2 waves) is the best choice. While T02 is small, it carries its own distinct set of acceptance criteria — guest-specific password, idempotent role update, no collection reassignment, and 10k credits — that deserve focused implementation and testing. Merging T02 into T01 (Option B) would save one developer handoff but at the cost of mixing schema concerns with seed-data concerns in a single task, making code review less focused. The parallel execution of T02 and T03 in Wave 1 is a minor bonus (T02 is fast), but maintaining clean task boundaries aligns with the project's established pattern of small, single-responsibility tasks. There are no technical blockers or architectural concerns that would justify deferral (Option C). The feature is well-scoped: only two role values ('admin'/'guest'), no complex permission matrix, full backward compatibility via default='admin', and all required infrastructure (auth, seed-users CLI, frontend Layout with beta section, i18n) already exists.

actions.notes: Proceed with 3-task / 2-wave plan as specified in F139-README.md. Wave 0: T01 (role column + schema + API + frontend type). Wave 1: T02 (seed guest user) + T03 (frontend beta access control) in parallel. No new external dependencies required. Migration via ALTER TABLE (same pattern as F99). Guest password hardcoded as 'mudar@12345' per user specification.
